title: Pagination
description: Cursor pagination for collection endpoints. Keyset/cursor based, never offset based: an offset over a mutating authoritative collection silently skips or repeats rows, which is unacceptable for order and ledger reads (docs/15, docs/02 section 9).

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. A server-defined maximum applies; an over-limit request is clamped or rejected, never silently truncated without a signal.

cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a previous response. Opaque to the client: its internal structure is not a contract and must not be parsed by callers.

x-invariants: Cursors are opaque. A client that parses one is depending on an unspecified implementation detail.
A cursor is bound to the query it was issued for. Reusing a cursor across a different filter set is rejected rather than reinterpreted.
For an authoritative collection, ordering defaults to descending by the authoritative sequence so that the newest state is never skipped.
A cursor encodes position, never authorization. It is not a capability and grants no access.
